comparison_basis.expected_completion_time: ordinal from tested operation count/remaining unknowns
comparison_basis.success: tested PASS where available; otherwise source-qualified plausibility only
comparison_basis.conflict_risk: whether stale/concurrent completion can create partial or duplicate visible state
comparison_basis.quota_fragility: accepted route must not require optional finite hosted quota

candidates.mechanism: Git Data transaction capsule: precreate content-addressed blobs, one combined tree, one commit, force=false ref publication, stale-parent full reconstruction, duplicate SHA-set no-op
candidates.evidence: live PASS 9/9 two-file stale-conflict fixture; separate raw binary write fixture
candidates.success: high within tested small role-local repo scope
candidates.conflict_risk: low in tested scope; live non-fast-forward conflict failed closed and fresh-base rebuild preserved intervening change
candidates.quota_fragility: low; constant-count lightweight Git repository API transport
limitations: arbitrary binary content readback through current connector is not byte-faithful

candidates.mechanism: canonical base16 identity-addressed UTF-8 chunks + manifest
candidates.success: high within tiny bounded payload scope
candidates.conflict_risk: low with immutable chunks and manifest CAS
limitations: does not itself create raw binary file

candidates.mechanism: thread-scoped Gmail draft-send reconciliation for existing-thread replies
candidates.evidence: official draft/thread semantics plus current read-thread connector; no live send
limitations: successful send destroys draft and creates new message ID
absence of sent op_id is not source-proven safe non-send evidence
violates zero optional quota or no-residual-execution constraints

decision: The Git Data transaction capsule is the strongest tested transversal mechanism in this run because one zero-hosted-compute pattern covered raw byte writes, atomic multi-file visibility, content identity, and stale publication recovery. Canonical text chunks remain the stronger readable state format when future Chat must inspect exact bytes. Opaque external sends and arbitrary environment-sensitive execution remain separate unresolved classes.
